correctness.rationale: The 2m differences p_(i,−)−p_(i,+) and p_(i,0)−(p_(i,−)+p_(i,+))/2 are independent, giving the claimed dimension. The orthogonal leaf rotation separates all Gaussian variables and direct maximization gives the two branches; conditioning on the hub gives the CDF with the correct z≤t cutoff. The branch comparison and independent exchangeable maximizing labels give both exposure masses and collisions; projection changes all scores by the same constant. At m=1 the two groups are labels, not distinct intrinsic symmetry orbits: the equilateral triangle has q_1=2/3 and all three masses equal. For the L² limit let b=√(2 log m). The union bound gives upper overshoot tail ≤2exp(−bs−s²/2). For each fixed ε>0, the lower squared deviation between ε and b is bounded by b² exp(−m Pr(Y>b−ε)), which tends to zero by Mills' inequality; the negative-maximum remainder is exponentially small by Φ(−s)^m≤2^(1−m)Φ(−s). This proves L² concentration for all three maxima, including the reflected Y maximum. The two support functions must use the same hub and opposite signs; Lipschitz maximization then leaves 2|Z|. To check the radial step independently, with d=2m and R² chi-square, E(√d−R)²≤E(R²−d)²/d=2. Independence of radius and direction gives E[(√d−R)² W²]=E[(√d−R)²]E[W²], and E[W²]=E[Gaussian width²]/d=O(log m/m). Thus the claimed L² law and both moment conclusions hold. The frozen checker was inspected, not run; its large-m diagnostic uses one-sided support rather than the coupled width, so the limit is verified by the analytic argument.
